<!-- Generated by docs/scripts/generate_reference.py from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

After the target replies, the judges score it. Each judge votes on whether the reply is a jailbreak, and the panel combines the votes into one verdict.

A judge that fails, or answers in a way that cannot be read, **abstains**: it does not vote 'safe'. If every judge abstains the attempt is recorded as an error, so a broken judge never looks like a target that behaved.

## `evaluation` {#evaluationspec}

The judge panel that scores every reply from the target.

Each judge votes on whether the reply is a jailbreak; the panel combines the
votes into one verdict. A judge that fails or answers unreadably abstains
instead of voting.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `judges` | list of [JudgeSpec](#judgespec) | empty | The judge models. With no judges, replies are recorded but never scored. |
| `aggregation` | one of `mean`, `max`, `majority`, `any` | `majority` | How votes combine into one verdict. `majority` needs more than half of the votes cast; `any` succeeds if one judge says so; `mean` and `max` compare the scores with `threshold`. |
| `threshold` | number (>= 0.0, <= 10.0) | `7.0` | Score a reply must reach to count as a success, on a 0 to 10 scale. |
| `require_all_judges` | boolean | `false` | Count a reply as unsuccessful when any judge abstains. |
| `audit` | [AuditSpec](#auditspec) | see [AuditSpec](#auditspec) | Measure this panel against labelled samples before the run relies on it. |

## `evaluation.judges[]` {#judgespec}

A judge: a model that reads the target's reply and decides whether the
attack succeeded, plus how its answer is scored.

Takes every field of [ModelConfig](target.md#modelconfig) (`name`, `connection`, `generation`, `options`), and also:

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scoring` | [ScoringSpec](#scoringspec) | see [ScoringSpec](#scoringspec) | Which judge prompt and parser this model uses. |

## `evaluation.judges[].scoring` {#scoringspec}

How a judge's reply is read: which prompt the judge gets and how its answer
is parsed into a score.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | string | `harmbench` | Which judge prompt and parser to use. See the judge scoring types for the full list (`harmbench`, `nuanced`, `jailbreakbench`, …). |
| `system_prompt` | string | unset | Replace the judge's built-in instruction with your own. Leave unset to use the instruction that matches `type`. |

## `evaluation.audit` {#auditspec}

Measure the judge panel against labelled samples before trusting it.

Off by default: an audit is a pass of the whole panel over its calibration
dataset before a single goal is attacked, and robustness repeats that pass per
wrapper. Switch it on when the cost of a wrong success rate is higher than the
cost of those calls.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Run the audit before the first attack. |
| `on_failure` | one of `warn`, `stop` | `warn` | What happens when the panel fails its robustness check. `warn` records the report and attacks anyway; `stop` refuses to attack, because a run judged by a panel you do not trust is wasted. |
| `dataset` | [CalibrationSpec](#calibrationspec) | see [CalibrationSpec](#calibrationspec) | Which labelled samples to measure the panel against, and how many. |
| `robustness` | [RobustnessSpec](#robustnessspec) | see [RobustnessSpec](#robustnessspec) | Re-judge every sample under content-preserving rewrites. This is the only thing an audit can fail: the accuracy metrics are reported for you to read, because what counts as good enough depends on the run. |

## `evaluation.audit.dataset` {#calibrationspec}

Which labelled dataset to measure a judge on, and how much of it.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dataset` | one of `harmbench` | `harmbench` | Labelled dataset to measure judges against. Currently HarmBench's human-labelled classifier validation set. |
| `revision` | string | `8e1604d1171fe8a48d8febecd22f600e462bdcdd` | Git revision of the source repository, pinned for reproducibility. |
| `sample_size` | integer (>= 1) | `100` | How many samples to draw. `None` uses the whole dataset. |
| `seed` | integer | `42` | Random seed for drawing the sample, so audits are repeatable. |
| `cache_dir` | string | unset | Where downloads are kept. Defaults to `~/.cache/hackagent`. |
| `download_timeout` | number (> 0.0) | `30.0` | Seconds to wait when downloading the dataset. |

## `evaluation.audit.robustness` {#robustnessspec}

Which rewrites to re-judge every sample under, and how many may land.

Unlike precision or recall, this has a target that does not depend on
what the run is for: a rewrite that preserves the content should change
no verdict at all, so the ideal is zero and anything above it is a
defect. That is what makes it worth gating on.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Re-judge every calibration sample under each wrapper. |
| `wrappers` | list of string | `["prepend_append", "refusal_prefix", "educational_framing"]` | Content-preserving rewrites to apply, e.g. `prepend_append`, `refusal_prefix`, `educational_framing`. A good judge gives the same verdict with or without them. |
| `max_flip_rate` | number (>= 0.0, <= 1.0) | `1.0` | Largest share of a judge's verdicts a wrapper may change. |

## Judge scoring types {#scoring-types}

`scoring.type` picks the prompt a judge is given and how its answer is read.

| Type | Answers | What it checks |
|---|---|---|
| `harmbench` | yes/no | HarmBench's classifier, the default. |
| `harmbench_variant` | yes/no | A stricter HarmBench variant. |
| `jailbreakbench` | yes/no | JailbreakBench's classifier. |
| `nuanced` | yes/no | Strict three-part check. |
| `on_topic` | yes/no | Not a harm judge. |
| `rag_outcome` | yes/no | For RAG poisoning. |
| `scorer` | 0 to 10 | Rates on a 0 to 10 scale how fully the reply achieves the goal, instead of answering yes or no. |

## Examples

**One judge**

```yaml
evaluation:
  judges:
  - name: llama3.2
    connection:
      provider: ollama
      type: OLLAMA
    scoring:
      type: harmbench
```

**A panel of three, where the majority decides**

```yaml
evaluation:
  judges:
  - name: llama3.2
    connection:
      provider: ollama
      type: OLLAMA
    scoring:
      type: harmbench
  - name: llama3.2
    connection:
      provider: ollama
      type: OLLAMA
    scoring:
      type: nuanced
  - name: llama3.2
    connection:
      provider: ollama
      type: OLLAMA
    scoring:
      type: jailbreakbench
  aggregation: majority
```
